intro: Ten stories from the last day, rewritten in plain British English. Tap any word you don't know.

items.title: Spain train crash: computer fault blamed
items.text: The death toll from the high-speed train crash near Toledo has risen to 69. Transport Minister Óscar Puente said a computer malfunction disabled a security system. He said controllers let a Renfe train go ahead without speed limits while an Iryo train was standing still in front of it. He added that this broke the rules. Fifty-seven injured people were still in hospital on Thursday, and Spain has declared three days of national mourning.

gloss.death toll: the number of people who died in a disaster
gloss.breach: to break a rule or agreement
gloss.protocol: the official set of rules for how something must be done
gloss.national mourning: a period when a whole country shows sadness for people who died

items.title: Russian strike on Dnipro station kills 14
items.text: A Russian strike on a railway platform in the Ukrainian city of Dnipro has killed 14 people. They were waiting for a train to Zaporizhzhia. At least 19 people died across Ukraine on Thursday, including two teenage girls in Chernihiv and three people in a residential building in Poltava. President Zelenskyy condemned the attack and called for stronger sanctions on Russia. Talks mediated by the United States are expected to restart next month.

gloss.strike: an attack, usually from the air
gloss.residential: used for people to live in
gloss.condemn: to say publicly that something is very bad or wrong
gloss.sanctions: official punishments, usually limits on trade, against a country
gloss.mediate: to help two sides in a dispute reach an agreement

items.title: Healey's first Budget: wages up, banks pay more
items.text: Chancellor John Healey presented his first Budget on Wednesday. The National Living Wage will rise from £12.71 to £13.20 an hour. The bank surcharge will go up from 3% to 6% from January 2027 until March 2028. The Office for Budget Responsibility expects growth of 1.2% this year and inflation to average 3.1%. About 20 million households in council tax bands A to D will get a £100 gas payment this winter.

gloss.Chancellor: the government minister in charge of the country's money
gloss.surcharge: an extra amount of tax or payment added to the normal one
gloss.inflation: the rate at which prices rise over time
gloss.household: all the people who live together in one home
gloss.council tax: a local tax paid by people who live in a property in the UK

items.title: Everton beat Newcastle 3-1 in League Cup
items.text: Everton beat Newcastle United 3-1 in the English League Cup on Thursday. The match finished at full time with a two-goal margin for the home side. It was a disappointing result for Newcastle, who have now gone out of the competition. Elsewhere on Thursday, Frosinone beat Lecce 5-1 in Serie A, and Fiorentina drew 2-2 with Atalanta.

gloss.League Cup: an English knockout competition for clubs from the top four divisions
gloss.knockout: a type of competition where the loser of each match goes out
gloss.go out: to lose and leave a competition
gloss.score: to put the ball in the goal and win a point

items.title: Copa del Rey: big wins and a penalty shoot-out
items.text: Several big scores came in the first rounds of the Spanish Copa del Rey. Athletic Club won 6-1 away at Prat, and Osasuna beat Atlético Calatayud 6-0. Sevilla and Granada both won 3-0 against lower-league sides. In Numancia against Real Oviedo, the match finished 3-3 after extra time. Numancia then won 4-2 on penalties and went through to the next round.

gloss.extra time: additional minutes played when a match is level at the end of normal time
gloss.penalties: a way to decide a match when both teams have scored the same, with players shooting at the goal one by one
gloss.away: played at the other team's stadium
gloss.lower-league: playing in a division below the top one
gloss.go through: to move on to the next round of a competition

items.title: Scientists find way to make EV batteries lighter
items.text: Scientists have developed a new technology that could make batteries for electric cars smaller and lighter. The researchers also say the batteries could last longer. This could allow cars to travel further on a single charge. Range is one of the main worries for people who are thinking about buying an electric vehicle. The work was reported by ScienceDaily on Wednesday.

gloss.battery: a device that stores electrical power
gloss.long-lasting: working well for a long time
gloss.range: the distance a vehicle can travel before it needs more fuel or power
gloss.charge: the amount of electricity stored in a battery
gloss.electric vehicle: a car that runs on electricity instead of petrol

items.title: Daylight linked to lower dementia risk
items.text: A study of more than 87,000 adults has found a link between daytime light and brain health. People who were exposed to more bright light during the day showed a benefit. The headline finding is that spending less than 42 minutes in bright daylight was linked to a higher risk of dementia. The study shows a link only, and it does not prove that light prevents the illness.

gloss.dementia: an illness that affects memory and thinking, mostly in older people
gloss.exposure: the state of being in contact with something such as light
gloss.risk: the chance that something bad will happen
gloss.prove: to show that something is definitely true

items.title: Actor Patrick Stewart dies aged 86
items.text: The actor Sir Patrick Stewart has died at the age of 86, according to reports on Thursday. He was best known for playing Captain Jean-Luc Picard in Star Trek and Professor Charles Xavier in the X-Men films. His career lasted for many decades on stage, television and film, and he was widely admired for his deep voice. Reports say he was one of the best-known British actors of his generation.

gloss.career: the work a person does during their life
gloss.captain: the leader of a ship or its crew
gloss.generation: people born around the same time
gloss.widely: by many people in many places

items.title: Lagarde to leave the ECB early
items.text: Christine Lagarde will leave her job as president of the European Central Bank on 7 February, eight months before her term ends. She said the role requires neutrality. The early exit gives Europe time to choose a successor before France's presidential election. The bank also kept interest rates unchanged and warned that energy costs threaten to push up inflation. Klaas Knot and Pablo Hernández de Cos are seen as leading candidates.

gloss.term: the fixed period of time a person holds a job
gloss.neutrality: not supporting any side in a dispute
gloss.successor: a person who takes over a job from someone else
gloss.interest rate: the percentage charged for borrowing money
gloss.push up: to make something such as prices rise

items.title: GTA VI: PS5 headset and new gameplay
items.text: PlayStation will release its new Pulse wireless headset on 19 November, the same day as Grand Theft Auto VI. Pre-orders opened on 29 October, and the headset costs £89.99. Rockstar Games has also shown new GTA VI gameplay, the first since August, in an episode of South Park. Reports say review codes have been sent to the press, with a review embargo on 18 November. Rockstar has not confirmed that date.

gloss.headset: a pair of headphones with a microphone, used for gaming and calls
gloss.pre-order: to ask to buy something before it is on sale
gloss.gameplay: the way a game looks and feels when you play it
gloss.review embargo: a date before which journalists must not publish their reviews
gloss.confirm: to say officially that something is true
